t: You're at Highgate Cemetery in north London, a Grade I listed place of burial designed by Stephen Geary. About 170,000 people lie in around 53,000 graves across the West and East sides, and it also works as a de facto nature reserve. The famous names here are wide-ranging. Michael Faraday, whose discoveries underpin electromagnetic induction, is buried here. So are the novelist George Eliot, author of Middlemarch, and John Galsworthy, who wrote The Forsyte Saga. Herbert Spencer, who coined the phrase survival of the fittest, is here too. So are Douglas Adams, creator of The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, and the singer George Michael.
